title: SLA-aware priority mapping for streamed chat + tool-chains with cost/latency budgets
creator: Lina Gomez
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers are submitting feature requests that combine streaming chat, multi-step tool/function calls, and structured outputs. Current intake labels these as single "requests" but lacks a deterministic way to map them to priority tiers given SLA constraints, tenant contracts, and per-token cost budgets. This leads to inconsistent triage outcomes and manual gatekeeping by PMs and SEs.

Goal: Define and implement a priority-mapping rubric and intake metadata fields that let the hosted API intake pipeline automatically surface: (1) SLA tier (response-time SLO vs throughput), (2) cost/latency budget sensitivity, (3) tool-chain complexity (number + statefulness of tool calls), and (4) fallback tolerance for structured outputs during degraded capacity. The rubric should be actionable for both self-serve intake and sales-assisted escalations.
proposal:
1) Extend intake form to capture: SLA tier, expected 95th latency target, estimated tokens-per-request, expected use of streaming, number of tool/function calls, structured-output schema tightness (strict/lenient), and fallback-allowed (boolean).
2) Build a priority-mapping function (PMF) that outputs an initial triage bucket: Critical-SLA, Enterprise-High, Enterprise-Medium, Self-Serve, Deferred. PMF takes into account contractual SLA, estimated cost impact, and tool-chain complexity.
3) Add an automated reviewer step that flags requests for an SE review if PMF marks High or Critical-SLA or if tool-chain complexity > 3.
4) Publish a decision matrix and customer-facing guidance so sales and SEs can set expectations during onboarding.
5) Wire outputs into the intake dashboard and telemetry to measure accuracy vs final disposition.
acceptance_criteria:
- Intake form updated in onboarding flow with the new fields and validation.
- PMF prototype implemented as a serverless function behind intake with deterministic outputs for a test set of 50 historical tickets.
- Dashboard shows automated bucket for incoming requests and a reason code.
- Triage accuracy >= 85% vs historical manual triage on a 100-ticket holdout.
- SE review workflow triggers work items automatically for High/Critical buckets.
- Public guidance doc published in Confluence and linked in intake flow.
success_metrics:
- Reduction in manual triage time per ticket by 40%.
- Time-to-first-response for Critical-SLA tickets <= 48h from intake.
- Decrease in mis-routed enterprise requests by 70% after launch.
- Adoption: >= 90% of new enterprise intake submissions include the new fields.
timeline:
Week 1: finalize rubric and intake form fields.
Week 2: implement intake form + validation and PMF prototype.
Week 3: run retrospective mapping on historical tickets, tune weights.
Week 4: dashboard + SE workflow + docs.
Week 5: soft launch with a cohort of 10 enterprise customers and iterate.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: PMF overfit to historical requests and misclassifies new patterns. Mitigation: conservative thresholds and human-in-the-loop SE review for first 6 weeks.
- Risk: Sales/SEs bypass intake and submit via email. Mitigation: operationalize a lightweight intake-only API that SEs must use and track bypasses.
- Risk: Additional intake fields increase friction and reduce submission quality. Mitigation: progressive disclosure: only show advanced fields when "enterprise" toggle is set.
notes:
We should coordinate with the Console team to ensure triage buckets appear in per-tenant dashboards and that rollouts can be targeted by tenant. Also coordinate with Pricing to estimate per-request cost impact bands for common model choices.
Initial weight suggestions for PMF: SLA contract presence (+40), expected tokens-per-request (>2000 -> +30), streaming-enabled (+10), tool-chain length * 15, structured-output strictness +20.
